title: Perfusable Vascular Network with a Tissue Model in a Microfluidic Device
protocol: Design the pattern of the microfluidic device using commercially available software.
Transfer the design file to a micro pattern generator and load the tool with a chromium mask coated with positive photoresist.
Expose the positive photoresist in the pattern area using a micro pattern generator.
Develop the positive photoresist using the developer.
Rinse the mask with deionized water.
Etch the chromium in the exposed area where the positive photoresist was removed.
Rinse the mask again with deionized water.
Remove remaining photoresist on the mask using acetone.
Prepare a clean silicon wafer (4 inch, P(100)).
Spin coat hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Softbake HMDS for 5 minutes at 120 °C and cool the wafer for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Spincoat the negative photoresist at 500 rpm for 10 seconds and then at 1,200 rpm for 30 seconds.
Prebake the negative photoresist for 45 min at 95 °C.
Cool the wafer for 60 min at room temperature.
Check the UV light intensity in each experiment.
Calculate the exposure time for a total exposure energy dose of 250 mW/cm².
Place the photomask on the wafer and expose it to UV light.
Postbake the negative photoresist for 1 min at 65 °C.
Postbake the negative photoresist for 5 min at 95 °C.
Allow the wafer to cool down for 1 min at room temperature.
Develop the negative photoresist layer in the first developer bath for 15 min.
Develop the negative photoresist layer in the second developer bath for 2 min.
Rinse the wafer in the first isopropanol (IPA) bath for 10 s.
Rinse the wafer in the second IPA bath for 10 s.
Hardbake the negative photoresist at 200 °C for 30 min.
Cool the wafer for 5 min at room temperature.
Measure the thickness of the negative photoresist layer using a surface profiler.
Place the wafer in a desiccator connected to a vacuum pump.
Add 200 μL of silane (trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane) to the desiccator.
Turn on the pump for 10 min.
Keep the wafer in the desiccator for 4 h after turning off the pump.
Cast the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) pre-polymer with a PDMS base:curing agent ratio of 10:1 (w/w).
Degas the casted PDMS in a vacuum chamber for 2 h.
Cure the PDMS at 80 °C in an air-vented oven overnight.
Peel off the cured PDMS from the silicon wafer.
Punch holes 1A - 3B with a 2-mm diameter punch.
Punch the spheroid culture well with a 1-mm diameter punch.
Clean the PDMS slab and glass cover slip with adhesive tape by repeatedly sticking and peeling off the tape.
Treat the PDMS slab with air plasma for 40 seconds (40 mW, 50 sccm).
Bond the PDMS slab onto the glass cover slip to expel any air bubbles between the surfaces.
Cure the bonded PDMS slab at 80 °C for at least 12 hours.
Thaw RFP-HUVECs and human lung fibroblasts (hLF) as per protocol.
Add thawed cells into endothelial cell and fibroblast medium, respectively.
Culture sub-confluent RFP-HUVECs and hLFs in a 100-mm dish at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2-3 days.
Detach RFP-HUVECs and hLFs from dishes with 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA.
Stop the trypsin reaction with 4 mL of DMEM containing 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 220 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend RFP-HUVECs in endothelial medium to a final concentration of 2.5 × 10^4 cells/mL.
Resuspend hLFs in endothelial medium to a final concentration of 1.0 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Gently add 200 µL of RFP-HUVECs cell suspension (containing 5,000 cells) per well in a 96-well plate.
Gently add 200 µL of hLFs cell suspension (containing 20,000 cells) per well in a 96-well plate.
Incubate the 96-well plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2-4 days.
NOTE: Perform spheroid loading on ice to prevent gelation of collagen and fibrin.
Dissolve fibrinogen in PBS for a final concentration of 2.80 mg/mL.
Prepare neutralized collagen (3.0 mg/mL in PBS) according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Combine 107.2 µL of fibrinogen solution (2.80 mg/mL) per reaction in a tube.
Add 8.0 µL of neutralized collagen (3.0 mg/mL) to the tube.
Mix 3.6 µL of aprotinin (5 U/mL) into the tube.
Label the prepared solution as "master mix solution" (MS).
Dissolve thrombin in PBS for a final concentration of 50 U/mL.
Thaw aliquots of 50 U/mL thrombin (20 µL/tube) stored at −30 °C before each experiment.
Place the 96-well plate containing the spheroids inside the biosafety cabinet.
Prepare two 35-mm Petri dishes inside the biosafety cabinet, with one dish on ice and the other on the benchtop.
Pipette 99 µL of MS at the center of the cold dish to form a droplet.
Trim the tips of 2 yellow pipette tips (10-100 µL) for collecting spheroids from the 96-well plate.
Cut the tips of 3 clear pipette tips (1-100 µL) for mixing thrombin with MS, precise collection of the spheroids, injecting the spheroids into the device, and injecting media into the device.
Ensure the pore size of the tips is slightly larger than the diameter of holes or wells to fit snugly.
Collect a spheroid with 100 µL of medium from the 96-well plate.
Add the collected spheroid to the Petri dish on the benchtop.
Pick up the spheroid with minimum volume of media from dish 2 using a pipettor.
Hold the pipettor upright so that gravity moves the spheroid towards the bottom of the pipet tip.
Eject the spheroid by touching the pipet tip onto the meniscus of the MS droplet in dish 1.
Add 1 μL of thrombin (50 U/mL) and mix gently with a yellow pipet tip.
With the pipette set to 7 μL, pick up the spheroid and slowly place it into the spheroid well.
Incubate for 15 min at 37 °C for the gelation of fibrin.
Slowly inject the endothelial medium from holes 1A and 3A and fill channels 1 and 3 with media (20~30 μL/channel).
Place the device in a 100-mm dish with a wet Kimwipe to prevent evaporation of media from the device.
Place the device at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h to remove bubbles at the interface between the media and fibrin.
Thaw GFP-HUVECs (3.0 x 10^5 cells/vial) and add them to 10 mL of endothelial medium.
Culture GFP-HUVECs in a 100-mm dish at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2-3 days to reach sub-confluency.
Detach GFP-HUVECs from the dishes with 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA.
Stop the trypsin reaction with 4 mL of DMEM containing 10% (v/v) fetal bovine serum and 1% (v/v) penicillin/streptomycin.
Centrifuge GFP-HUVECs at 220 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend GFP-HUVECs in endothelial medium at a concentration of 5.0 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Inject HUVEC cell suspension (20 µL) into channel 1 through hole 1B.
Tilt the microfluidic device 90° and place it on its side.
Incubate the device at 37 °C for 30 min to allow HUVECs to adhere to fibrin in channel 2.
Confirm attachment of HUVECs at the interface between gel and medium.
Exchange half of the media in channels 1 and 3 daily.
Prepare 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.
Remove media from channels 1 and 3 and add 20 µL of 4% PFA per channel.
Repeat removal of solution and addition of 4% PFA three times.
Incubate the device at 4 °C overnight.
Remove 4% PFA from the device.
Wash channels three times with PBS.
Add 20 µL of 10 µg/mL fluorescent dye (Table of Materials) per channel to stain cellular nuclei.
Repeat removal of solution and addition of 10 µg/mL fluorescent dye three times.
Store the device at 4 °C for 24 h.
Prepare the spheroid after culturing for more than 7 days in the device at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the medium from holes 1A, 1B, 3A, and 3B.
Introduce 10 μL of 10 μM solution of FITC-dextran in PBS into holes 1A and 1B.
Monitor the flow of microbeads or FITC dye under an inverted microscope.
Overlap images of GFP-HUVECs days 0, 1, 3, 5, and 7.
Subtract the position of the vasculature tip on day 0 from the same position at images taken on days 1, 3, 5, and 7.
Determine the growth of the vascular tip from the root position to define sprout length.
Binarize the fluorescent images of the coculture spheroid containing RFP-HUVECs.
Measure "centroid" position by analysis function in ImageJ to determine the center of the spheroid.
Determine the position of the vascular tips and roots as done in step 7.
Measure the vascular angles using analysis function in ImageJ software.
